subject: Post-call: ShopLine workload splay & token crest qualification
message_1_subject: Post-call: ShopLine workload splay & token crest qualification
message_1_body:
Thanks for a productive call earlier — quick recap and our asks so we can size for pilot capacity. TL;DR: baseline QPS ~12, expected sustained token rate ~18k t/s, peak crest up to ~320k t/s across the fleet during promotions (short windows), typical request size ~1.5k tokens, occasional long requests up to 8k tokens (batch of user chat history + context).

Key SLOs you called out: 95th latency target <= 250ms for short responses (<512 tokens), streaming tail acceptable up to 500ms for long/streamed responses. Can you confirm these are the production SLOs we should model?

Operational constraints we noted:
- Must support server-sent streaming for multi-turn chat (client keeps connection ~30s).
- Concurrent live user sessions target: 60 concurrent streams at peak.
- Warm-start preference for sessions to avoid cold-kv fill latency spikes.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Share a sample token histogram or the CSV export you promised (we can consume shopline_token_profile.csv). Helps nail burst profile and dispatch policy.
2) Confirm monthly committed throughput target (tokens/month) vs on-demand headroom.
3) Any region-specific routing needs (we flagged us-west primary with eu fallback).

Attachments: I attached a simple CSV template (shopline_token_profile.csv) for the token distribution and a short Redwood sizing notes PDF that explains how we translate token crests to dedicated slot sizing.

Next steps: if you share the histogram we’ll run an ops-level sizing pass and propose a Dedicated pilot commit + fallback rules. Can we schedule a 45-minute follow-up on Mon 6/5 to review sizing output?

Thanks — Rishi

message_2_subject: Re: Post-call: ShopLine workload splay & token crest qualification
message_2_body:
Thanks Rishi — great summary. Confirming the SLOs you listed are accurate for the pilot: 95th <= 250ms short responses, streaming tail up to 500ms for long responses.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 320k t/s crest is across our entire fleet and typically lasts ~90–150s during flash promotions; the crest is geographically concentrated in US-West.
- The 60 concurrent streams number is our delta above baseline; baseline concurrent streams sit around 12.
- For region routing: prefer us-west primary, fall back to us-east; EU traffic is <2% for now.

I attached a cleaned export of the token histogram (shopline_token_profile.csv). The peak window rows are at the bottom — let us know if you need a different aggregation.

Also, can you send a short ops checklist of inputs you need (edge keepalive, max concurrent connections per IP, sticky session guidance) so our infra team can prep?

—Helen

message_3_subject: Re: Post-call: ShopLine workload splay & token crest qualification — ops checklist & initial sizing notes
message_3_body:
On Thu, Jun 2, 2028 at 9:12 AM Helen Park <helen@shopline.com> wrote:
> The 320k t/s crest is across our entire fleet and typically lasts ~90–150s during flash promotions; the crest is geographically concentrated in US-West.
> The 60 concurrent streams number is our delta above baseline; baseline concurrent streams sit around 12.

Thanks for the CSV Helen — useful data. A few ops inputs from our infra/serving side: (short checklist)
- Edge keepalive: recommend 65s TCP keepalive, HTTP/2 connection reuse; avoids frequent TLS handshakes for short streams.
- Max concurrent connections per client IP: 100 (but we can tune per-account).
- Session stickiness: not required; we use KV warm paths for affinity but can operate without sticky routing.
- Streaming chunk size: we stream with 256–512 token chunks to keep tail latency predictable.

Initial sizing notes (very high level):
- Baseline (sustained): QPS ~12; estimated sustained token rate ~18k tokens/sec mapped to a small dedicated pool (~2 slots on gpus with q4 quant).
- Crest windows: translating your 320k t/s crest across the region yields ~X dedicated slots (I attached redwood_sizing_notes.pdf with the conversion table). For a safe pilot we recommend burst capacity via on-demand plus a canary dedicated reserve to handle crests while we tune batching.

Action items for ShopLine infra team:
1) Confirm you can expose histogram CSV with 1s granularity for at least two promo events.
2) Share preferred maintenance window for a short ingress test (we can do a non-prod stress run).
3) Confirm whether long requests (8k tokens) will be broken into streaming chunks by your frontend or sent as a single POST.

I attached the sizing notes PDF we referenced previously. Rishi — happy to jump on the 6/5 sync and walk through the slot math.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Performance & Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
message_4_subject: Re: Post-call: ShopLine workload splay & token crest qualification — next steps and 6/5 sync

Confirmed inputs we have:

ShopLine asks we still need:

- A 1s-granularity export for at least two promo crest windows (for accurate crest shape).

On the pilot recommendation: we will propose a hybrid approach — small Dedicated reserve to maintain SLO for critical traffic + on-demand burst capacity to absorb unpredictable crests. That gives you predictable baseline economics and protects against early throttling.
